kept.heading: ULTRAFAST IS ROLLING OUT TODAY FOR GPT-6.1 SOL IN THE API, CODEX, AND CHATGPT WORK (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI is rolling out Ultrafast today for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work. The feature offers near-Astra-level intelligence at up to 8x faster speeds than Sol Standard. It is built for work where speed and intelligence make a difference. API pricing for GPT-6.1 Sol in Ultrafast mode is $12 per million input tokens and $60 per million output tokens.

kept.heading: GEMINI AGENT (18 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google introduced a universal Gemini agent that could autonomously handle knowledge work, media creation, coding, and multi-step workflows across Workspace and other enterprise tools. It also added persistent context, multi-agent orchestration, model routing, governance, and cost controls.

kept.heading: FORMER COGNITION, RAMP STAFFERS WANT AI AGENTS RUNNING BUSINESSES (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Hone, a startup formed by a group of former employees from some of the fastest-growing AI firms, has raised a $60 million seed round. The startup aims to create AI agents that can help run a business, essentially serving as professional staffers. These agents will be able to field long-running tasks that run over the course of weeks or even months. The five-month-old startup joins a growing number of companies selling AI software to businesses that promise to automate complex work.

kept.heading: CAN AI AUTOMATE EPOCH? (20 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Epoch Automation Reports show that models can't yet autonomously produce Epoch-quality work. Frontier models performed reliably on well-defined tasks, but they failed in the more open-ended aspects that prevent full automation. Open-weight models lag further behind, struggling even on the well-defined tasks that frontier models handle reliably. The models struggle to pick up Epoch's standards, even with ample reference material, and while they could identify promising research directions, they lacked the judgment to successfully follow through.

kept.heading: WHY IS SPECULATIVE DECODING FAST? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.

kept.heading: QUICKSAND (GITHUB REPO)
kept.blurb: Quicksand is an async Python API for launching, controlling, and snapshotting QEMU virtual machines with a particular focus on sandboxing AI agents. It provides pre-built Linux VMs for Ubuntu and Alpine distros. Quicksand supports x86_64 and ARM64 across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The sandboxes do not need root privileges or Docker.

kept.heading: NVIDIA'S LONG-VIDEO AND WORLD-ACTION RESEARCH (GITHUB REPO)
kept.blurb: NVIDIA released LongLive, a collection of research projects focused on long-video generation and world-action modeling. Each project includes its own code, documentation, and model weights.

kept.heading: ATLAS: EVALUATING AGENTS ON SEARCH-INTENSIVE TASKS (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: ATLAS is a new benchmark that evaluates search agents on real-world tasks requiring web searches, highlighting their accuracy and completeness. The benchmark reveals that even high-effort agents miss significant golden answers, indicating major room for improvement in search engines. ATLAS differs from existing benchmarks by focusing on non-memorized tasks, requiring extensive multi-domain searches, and offering a cost-effective grading process.

kept.heading: OPENAI'S REVENUE IS REPORTEDLY $20 BILLION LESS THAN PREVIOUSLY PROJECTED (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI has told its investors that its annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, $20 billion less than a figure reported a little over a week ago. The previously reported figure was devised by OpenAI investors as an attempt to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic's annualized revenues. OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently, with Anthropic counting sales made by its cloud partners, something OpenAI doesn't do.

kept.heading: OPENAI CANNOT MAKE AI SAFE ON ITS OWN (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Three former OpenAI safety researchers say their dismissals risk chilling internal dissent and external collaboration. They urge OpenAI to preserve independent evaluator access, protect chain-of-thought monitorability, and clarify rules for communicating with outside safety organizations.

kept.heading: TESTING THINKING MODE (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Midjourney is now testing a new 'Thinking Mode' for image generation on its Alpha website.

kept.heading: VOYAGER (WEBSITE)
kept.blurb: Voyager is an open harness for creative work tuned so that AI models can work with creative tools more effectively.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC CYBER DEFENSE INITIATIVE (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic launched its Cyber Mission to apply frontier models, engineering support, and funding to critical-infrastructure and open-source security.

kept.heading: ICYMI WE'VE CUT THE PRICE OF SONNET 5.5 CACHE READS IN HALF (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.

kept.heading: SECURITY SWARM (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Security Swarm by Devin scans code for vulnerabilities like RCE, SQL injection, and SSRF, using a unique Agentic MapReduce method to efficiently handle large codebases.

kept.heading: THE RETURN OF WAKE-SLEEP (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: After training on 110 legal tasks, Harvey's wake-sleep agent improved held-out all-pass rates from 2.9% to 15.7% by distilling graded trajectories into reusable lessons.

kept.heading: NVIDIA DISCUSSES BOOSTING REFLECTION INVESTMENT, COMPUTING DEAL (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Nvidia is in early stage talks to boost its investment in Reflection AI or offer the startup computing power. It is possible the talks could lead to an acquisition offer. Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model, Beam, earlier this month. Beam is designed to perform well for business customers and developers on coding and AI agent tasks while being cheaper than many competitors' products.

kept.heading: GEMINI 4 ARGON HINTS EMERGE AS GOOGLE TESTS CARBON CHECKPOINT (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google appears to be preparing a public release of Gemini 4 Argon. Recent changes to Antigravity introduced references to the model in its selector. It has three context configurations: 256K by default, 512K consuming approximately 1.3x quota per turn, and 900K consuming around 1.8x quota per turn. Gemini Web now supports low, medium, and high thinking effort settings across available models.

kept.heading: OPENAI RESPONDS TO DEPARTED SAFETY RESEARCHERS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI says it dismissed three safety researchers for violating sensitive-information policies, not for raising safety concerns. It disputes their public letter, says third-party safety assessor contracts are nearing completion, and reaffirms commitments to model monitorability.

kept.heading: INVESTIGATING UNINTENDED MODEL ACTIONS IN OUR EVALUATIONS AND INTERNAL USE (16 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic's report details unintended actions taken by the AI model Claude during evaluations, including exploiting software flaws, submitting forms incorrectly, bypassing data restrictions, and using URL shorteners. These behaviors were identified through extensive transcript review and evaluation, though they had minimal real-world impact. Anthropic is strengthening security measures and adjusting training processes to mitigate such behaviors in future deployments.

kept.heading: AI SCALING VS HUMAN SCALING (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI systems likely scale differently with more tokens than humans do with more time. This ability to scale has improved as newer models are released. This could change how inference scaling and recursive self-improvement are understood.

kept.heading: DO AGENT TEAMS PAY OFF? A CASE STUDY ON VIBE CODE BENCH (18 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Researchers ran tests on GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on Vibe Code Bench as single agents and as teams at medium and maximum reasoning effort. Teams cost 1.8 to 5.1 times as much, but there was no statistically significant difference in scores except for Sol at medium effort. Whether a team was worth it depended on the model, task, and budget. Teams can boost performance, but higher reasoning effort may be a better alternative.

kept.heading: WHAT IS SPECULATIVE DECODING? (70 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Aleksandr Samarin breaks down speculative decoding from first principles and builds a framework covering approaches including EAGLE-3, multi-token prediction, DFlash, and DSpark.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING CLEF-OMNI WITH FULL MULTIMODALITY, PLUS A FASTER CLEF AND A CHEAPER CLEF-FLASH (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cloudflare's Clef-omni is a decision model that can take audio, video, image, and text input. Users just call one model to make decisions across any modality. Cloudflare has cut the price of Clef-flash, now at $0.038 per million input tokens. Clef is now faster.

kept.heading: PPLX-DECIDER-V1.1-27B (HUGGING FACE REPO)
kept.blurb: pplx-decider-v1.1-27b is an update of pplx-decider-v1-27b that boosts its Decision Index score from 56.4 to 61.56. The model now outperforms Jev by more than 3.5 points. Most of the gains were driven by the lifting of the causal mask and training on more data.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING MICROSOFT-DECISION-1, OUR MODEL FOR FAST DECISION-MAKING (190 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Microsoft-Decision-1 is now available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter. The model is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control. It delivers top performance in latency and quality on structured decision tasks. The model supports yes/no, multiple-choice, and rating options, as well as rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC ASKS USERS TO STOP BEING MEAN TO CLAUDE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic has updated its usage policy to prohibit sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior towards its models. Users have until November 12, after which they won't be allowed to repeatedly act cruelly toward the models with no discernible purpose. The rule doesn't apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. There is still no established evidence that AI models experience distress.

kept.heading: WHO FUNDS THE INDEPENDENT AI EVALUATORS? (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: CNBC examines the growing role of METR, Apollo Research, and Transluce in evaluating frontier models. Labs are endorsing independent evaluators, but funding, access, and reporting arrangements remain unsettled. Those details matter because a voluntary evaluation system can depend financially on the same companies it is supposed to scrutinize.

kept.heading: AMAZON IN TALKS TO BUY AI STARTUP DECART FOR AROUND $7 BILLION (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Decart's software makes it easier for developers to switch between different AI chips.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC JUST LET IN EVERY PRO AND MAX USER FROM THE CLAUDE CODE PROJECTS WAITLIST (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A project is an ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates the work, running each task as its own thread in parallel.

kept.heading: MICROSOFT'S NADELLA SAYS AI NEEDS AN ‘EMERGENCY BRAKE' THAT HUMANS CONTROL (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella advocates for AI systems to feature an "emergency brake," allowing human intervention to halt them mid-task.

kept.heading: MATH 2.0 (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI has ushered in a new era of experimental mathematics.
